- Spike coincides with a deploy at ~14:35 UTC (canary -> prod)
- A small subset of requests show repeated retry loops (x2-3)
- We see long queuing delays on GPU workers (queue depth metric attached)

We need immediate help. Can you confirm you’re seeing the same and escalate to execs if necessary — our enterprise users are being hit.

Subject: Re: PrismAI: sudden latency & 5xx spike on inference-v2 — triage notes

Evan / team — quick triage update from runtime:

Findings:
- We observed a canary rollout that enabled a more aggressive batching window (default 30ms -> 150ms) for inference-v2. That increased queueing under the observed traffic mix and produced head-of-line blocking on a subset of GPU workers.
- A small regression in the sequencer back-pressure logic resulted in retry storms when requests hit the overloaded batch. Retries amplify queue depth and led to 5xx responses once worker accept queues filled.

Immediate mitigations applied (15:25–15:35 UTC):
- Reduced batching window to 20ms for inference-v2 (temporary, rollbackable).
- Disabled the canary's sequencer change (flagged as transient).
- Increased per-worker accept queue from 256 -> 512 until we stabilize.

Result: p95 latency dropped from ~1.2s to ~240ms and 5xx rate down to ~0.8% on the subset we’re monitoring. We still see some lingering retries but queuing is markedly improved.

Next steps (owner):
- Rishi / Runtime: push a small rollback patch to canary configuration and bake for 45m. Attachment: mitigation-patch-rollback.sh
- Laura / Capacity: evaluate short-term capacity bump or overflow routing to model-variant-c (compatible) to reduce customer traffic on crowded nodes.
- Monica: prepare customer-facing timeline and credit proposal.

Will update in 30 minutes with expanded metrics.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Evan / Gina / team —

Thanks again for working through this with us. Below is an executive summary you can share with your leadership, plus next-step asks.

Executive summary (one-line):
A canary configuration change to the batching window caused increased queueing and a retry amplification loop starting at ~14:35 UTC, elevating p95 latency and 5xx rates; we applied a temporary rollback and configuration fixes, and p95 is materially improved while we validate full remediation.

Timeline (high level):
- 14:35 UTC — Canary rollout enabled larger batching window
- 14:40 UTC — Customer-reported latency & 5xx spike (PrismAI)
- 15:25 UTC — Runtime mitigations applied (reduced batching window, disabled sequencer change, increased worker queues)
- 15:40–16:30 UTC — Metrics improved (p95 ~240ms, 5xx ~0.8%)
- 09:15 UTC (next day) — Ongoing validation; patch bake and plan for full rollback scheduled

Root cause: Aggressive canary batching window + sequencer back-pressure regression that produced head-of-line blocking for certain request shapes, amplified by client retries.

Current status:
- Partial mitigation in place; customer traffic is stabilizing on adjusted config.
- Patch to revert the canary change and harden sequencing logic is staged for rollout and will be baked for 45–60 minutes.

Proposed customer remedies (we recommend):
1) Full rollback of the canary config and sequencing fix (Rishi) — ETA to complete & validate: 60–90 minutes after approval.
2) Short-term overflow to model-variant-c for high-throughput traffic (Laura) — requires customer opt-in; lead time: immediate once we toggle routing policy.
3) Goodwill credit to cover impacted tokens during the incident window — Monica / Marissa to propose a credit and get procurement sign-off (proposed-credit-offer.md attached).

Ask of PrismAI execs:
- Approve the full rollback and the overflow routing option (reply-all with APPROVE / DECLINE).
- Confirm whether you want us to move forward with the proposed credit (we’ll CC contracts@prismai.com for formalization).

Attachments: incident-timeline.xlsx (one-page timeline), proposed-credit-offer.md (credit draft).

I’ll schedule a 30-minute exec touchpoint if you’d like to review the one-pager live — suggest 10:00 UTC. Please advise.
